summary: Long-context requests cause KV cache growth and autoscaler flapping in dedicated pool, leading to p99 latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed repeated p99 latency spikes and intermittent throughput drops on their dedicated pool. Spikes correlate with a small number of long-context chat sessions (40k-80k tokens) that appear to keep large KV caches pinned on GPU workers.

Impact:
- Customer ScribeAI reports degraded user experience (text generation p99 latency from ~220ms -> 2.1s) across multiple routes.
- Dedicated pool capacity oscillates: autoscaler scales up after sustained high GPU memory usage, then several large sessions end and cached state is evicted, freeing memory and causing a scale-down, repeating every ~15-30min.
- Other tenants on same pool see transient elevated latencies during scale events.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool id: dp-7e9c-us-east
- Region: us-east-1 (prod)
- Node type: A100-80GB (mixed v1/v2)
- Observed models: redwood/falcon-65b-v2 pinned by customer for routing

Why this is different from other noisy-neighbor reports:
- Not pure noisy CPU or GPU kernel saturation. The primary signal is large KV cache residency per-session (per-tenant) and the autoscaler's current decision signals (GPU memory usage + pod count) treat resident cache as sustained load, triggering scaling behavior that then exposes ephemeral freeing of memory and a follow-up downscale. This creates a feedback loop that's not addressed by simple rate-limiting or tenant throttling.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a dedicated pool with mixed long/short stream tenants (simulate with loadgen).
Open 5-10 concurrent sessions that stream progressively to reach 40k-80k tokens context each and keep them active (idle but pinned) for 20-30 minutes.
Run a background steady stream of short requests from other tenants to observe p99 of short requests.
Observe GPU memory usage, per-session KV cache size, and autoscaler scale events in the window 00:10-00:40.
Correlate p99 latency spikes with scale up/down events and KV cache resident size per worker.
logs: Mar 01 09:12:04 metrics: dp-7e9c-us-east node-17 gpu_mem_used=72GB gpu_mem_total=80GB kv_cache_resident=38GB
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Not a kernel hang or OOM; GPUs remain healthy and temperature normal. No driver resets observed.
KV cache metric exists but autoscaler doesn't currently account for 'logical' pinned memory vs active compute footprint. The metric used is total GPU memory usage.
Per-tenant KV cache sizes: ScribeAI sessions showing ~30-45GB resident per long session on A100-80GB nodes.
Autoscaler window is 10min with hysteresis tuned for throughput; long-idle pinned caches trigger perceived sustained memory pressure for ~12-20min causing scale decisions.
When cached sessions terminate or drop to inactive, eviction frees memory quickly and a downscale happens within the next policy window, creating 15-30 minute oscillations.
Other mitigation attempts: temporarily moving ScribeAI traffic to isolated pool (manual routing) removed the p99 spikes for other tenants but didn't resolve root cause.
Hypothesis: autoscaler should be cache-aware (differentiate resident KV cache vs active compute) or we should expose per-tenant soft caps to avoid unbounded cache residency on shared pools.
Observed that smaller VMs (v1 nodes) are more susceptible to immediate pressure due to fragmentation and per-session slot allocation behavior.
Related historical issues: linked SUP-50385 (microthrottling), SUP-77109 (throughput drift) — similar downstream effects but different primary cause.
comments: Support (Marisol Alvarez, 2026-03-01 09:55): Acknowledged from customer; collecting logs and asked SRE to pull node-level kv_cache metrics. Customer provided sample session IDs: scribe-ctx-1 / scribe-ctx-7.

SRE (Ethan Kim, 2026-03-01 11:30): Confirmed autoscaler events correlate with memory spikes. Will instrument per-session KV residency metric in monitoring and add a dashboard. Assigned to investigate autoscaler decision logic.

Customer (ScribeAI - Priya Rao, 2026-03-01 12:05): Noted that long sessions are expected; they rely on keeping conversation context for UX. Asked about immediate workarounds — willing to accept routing to a dedicated isolated pool temporarily.

Support (Marisol Alvarez, 2026-03-01 12:40): Implemented temporary route pinning for ScribeAI to a warm isolated pool (dp-iso-03). Observed immediate reduction in cross-tenant p99 spikes. Noted to customer as a stopgap.

Eng (Runtime - Ashok Menon, 2026-03-02 09:15): Proposal: introduce 'kv_cache_resident_bytes' signal into autoscaler decision and a separate threshold that treats resident cache > X as soft-cap rather than hard trigger for scale-up. Also propose per-tenant cache soft-limits as config.

SRE (Ethan Kim, 2026-03-03 16:00): Deployed temporary alert: 'kv-cache-resident-crossing-tenant-threshold' for dp-7e9c-us-east. Added per-pool metric panels. Planning next: A/B test autoscaler change in staging.
Support (Marisol Alvarez, 2026-03-05 08:00): Customer accepted temporary isolated pool routing and requested timeline for permanent mitigation. Notified that ETA for PR review is ~1 week.

Eng (Ashok Menon, 2026-03-05 18:20): Opened RFC and PR targeting autoscaler change: treat kv_cache_resident_bytes as transient unless sustained over 60min and add per-tenant soft cap enforcement. PR link attached above.
resolution: Workaround: Manually routed ScribeAI to an isolated dedicated pool (dp-iso-03) on 2026-03-01 to stop noisy impact on other tenants.

Short-term mitigation: Added monitoring and an alert for per-tenant kv cache resident bytes; created dashboard for dp-7e9c-us-east. Added guidance to Customer Success for pinning high-context customers to isolated pools.

Planned permanent fix: Autoscaler change to incorporate 'kv_cache_resident_bytes' with a longer evaluation window (60min) and logic to avoid scale-up solely on pinned cache. Add per-tenant soft caps and eviction policy when cache exceeds configurable threshold.

Follow-ups: Backport autoscaler change to previously impacted pools, create a runbook for operators to identify long-context cache issues, and add SDK guidance for customers on expected cost/behavior for long pinned sessions.
Owner: Engineering (Ashok Menon) timeline: PR in review, expected rollout to staging 2026-03-10, production rollout targeted 2026-03-17 pending testing.
Status: In Progress — mitigation applied; permanent fix in development.
